source: Zieba et al. (2022), Astronomy & Astrophysics 664, A79, 'K2 and Spitzer phase curves of the rocky ultra-short-period planet K2-141 b hint at a tenuous rock vapor atmosphere' (doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202142912; arXiv:2203.00370). Spitzer IRAC channel 2 (4.5 um), 65 hours over 10 orbits between UT 2018 October 9 and 11, program 14135. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source, their table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, column 'Sinusoidal (phi = 0)', the model the BIC prefers for those data (Delta BIC 8.8 over a free offset). The text calls A the peak-to-trough amplitude. The paper prints no temperature for this model; the dayside temperature below is the same table's two-temperature fit to the same Spitzer data, the paper's only Spitzer-only dayside brightness temperature, and is used to fix the star's band temperature.

radiusRatio.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Sinusoidal (phi = 0), R_p/R_*

eclipseDepth.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Sinusoidal (phi = 0), f_p/f_*

model.equation: A sinusoid of peak-to-trough amplitude A times an eclipse model of depth f_p/f_*, with the hot spot offset fixed at 0 (section 3.1, model 2).

semiAmplitude.cell: A = 120.6 +42.3 -43.0 ppm peak to trough: half of it is the semi-amplitude, 60.3 ppm
semiAmplitude.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Sinusoidal (phi = 0), A; abstract, 'a peak to trough amplitude variation'

offsetDegreesEast.cell: fixed at 0; with the offset free, -34.5 +15.3 -14.6 degrees (west), which the BIC does not prefer
offsetDegreesEast.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Sinusoidal (phi = 0) and (phi free)

daysideK.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Two Temp., T_p,d

nightsideK.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Two Temp., T_p,n

offsetDegrees.where: table of models fitted to the Spitzer data alone, Sinusoidal (phi = 0)
